text:
Maya Chen: FYI customer escalation from Greenline — just after the March rollout they're seeing markdown/code-block formatting regressions. code fences are getting extra backticks and sometimes the closing fence is missing.

Greenline (customer): reproducer pasted below — this used to return a clean code block, now it sometimes returns an extra backtick and breaks the renderer. customer says it started ~ right after your canary. their app is hitting this in prod.

Greenline (customer): ```
Request body (abbreviated):
POST /v1/outputs
{
  "model": "rw/clarion-13b:v3.2.1",
  "input": "Create a markdown README with example:
```
console.log('hello')
```
",
  "stop": ["```"],
  "max_new_tokens": 150
}

Response they received:
{
  "output": "# README
Example:
```javascript
console.log('hello')
````

Some text after.
(there's an extra backtick after the closing fence)"
}
```

Maya Chen: They've pasted screenshots where our renderer (and their downstream MD parser) chokes because there is a 4th backtick or the closing fence is missing entirely. They also saw cases where inline triple backticks are replaced by literal `\``` tokens in the output.

Maya Chen: Can we triage? Customer is threatening to throttle usage until we confirm a fix (they rely on consistent markdown output). INC-2241 created in our tracker.

deploy-bot: Deployment rw/clarion-13b:v3.2.1 rollout started 2026-03-05T03:10:12Z (canary->70%).

Owen Patel: I'm jumping in. First suspects: stop-sequence handling or decoder post-processing change in the runtime that landed as part of the rollout. Priya, any recent tokenizer/decoder changes that could affect delimiter tokens?

Priya Rao: Looking. Quick notes: we shipped a change to "preserve_stop_sequence_tokens" logic in the compilation layer (commit 7b2f9) — it was meant to preserve stop tokens in the output for some legacy clients. It might interact badly with our markdown postprocessors. Also there was a small change to strip trailing repeated delimiter tokens for streaming in commit 7b3a1, but that was reverted in unit tests; maybe canary didn't pick up revert.

Sam Ortiz: Can you repro locally on a pinned model? If it's a model-side generation behavior we should be able to replicate with the same model artifact.

Owen Patel: Reproducer (local curl):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/outputs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw/clarion-13b:v3.2.1","input":"Create a markdown README with example:\n```\nconsole.log(\'hello\')\n```\n","stop":["```"],"max_new_tokens":150}'
```

Owen Patel: I ran that against canary; I see the extra backtick in ~20% of responses. Against the pinned v3.2.0 (pre-rollout) it returns clean fences. So this is a regression introduced in v3.2.1 or in the rollout runtime change.

Priya Rao: Confirmed on my side with sampled seeds. Hypothesis: certain internal token IDs (the token we use to represent fence delimiter) are being emitted twice when the preserved-stop-token flag is set, and our sanitizer later tries to strip but sometimes leaves an extra char when a streaming chunk boundary aligns with the fence. Two interacting bugs: (1) stop-token preservation, (2) chunk/truncation handling in streaming.

Maya Chen: Customer impact: markdown rendering broken -> UI shows broken code blocks for some generated docs. They're seeing this on about 10–15% of produced docs per their logs.

Sam Ortiz: Short-term mitigation options:
- Force clients to pass stop sequences explicitly (they already do, but we can add server-side extra trimming for triple backticks), or
- Pin Greenline to rw/clarion-13b:v3.2.0 (pre-rollout) — quick but not ideal, or
- Flip runtime feature flag that enables the new preserve-stop-token behavior (if reversible) to false for affected backends.

Owen Patel: I can flip the feature flag for the hosted cluster for Greenline's tenant and other affected accounts. That will be a config-level rollback with minimal infra risk. If that isn't possible fast enough, we can pin their API key to the older model version.

Priya Rao: Root cause writeup (short): commit 7b2f9 changed how stop tokens are returned to clients to support legacy clients expecting the delim. The streaming assembler code didn't account for emitting a partial token at a chunk boundary, resulting in duplicated delimiter characters in the final concatenated output. The model artifact itself is okay, but the runtime/assembler change is what made the delimiter handling visible.

Maya Chen: Action items:
- Sam to flip flag for production default back to old behavior for hosted API (rollback preserve-stop-token).
- Owen to create a pin for Greenline to v3.2.0 if flag flip is delayed.
- Priya to prepare a unit/regression test and a fix for the streaming assembler; target hotfix to eng-runtime.
- CS: Communicate workaround to customer and set expectation (ETA 24–48h).

Sam Ortiz: Flag flip scheduled now; I'll monitor errors and sampling for any side effects. (done)

Sam Ortiz: Quick update: after flipping the flag at 2026-03-05T12:24Z for the hosted cluster, I sampled 200 outputs with the same prompt — 0 failures in the sample. Greenline please confirm.

Greenline (customer): Confirmed — initial tests look good on their side, code blocks are rendering correctly again. Thanks.

Priya Rao: I'll open PR with fix for assembler (adds explicit join + sanitizer for delimiter sequences) and attach regression tests. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/4823

Owen Patel: We'll include a small canary for the fix and ensure the preserver flag change doesn't reintroduce the issue.

Maya Chen: I'll update INC-2241 with the mitigation and mark as partially mitigated — waiting for permanent fix to be merged and rolled out.

Priya Rao: Final note for postmortem: add a test that generates markdown fences at streaming chunk boundaries and assert triplet fences are stable. Also add a telemetry alert for sudden increases in newline/backtick anomalies.

Maya Chen: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the customer thread and keep this open until PR is live and rolled. :thumbsup:
